title: $\iota$-real and $\iota$-realizable Weil sheaves
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, fix
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in
[def-weil-punctual-weights], and let $\mathcal F$ be a
constructible
Weil sheaf on $X_0$, with the
stalk Frobenius modules $(V_x,F_x)$ of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Reality is a pointwise condition on
those modules, so the definition is stated for constructible sheaves; the
lisse case is the classical one, and is the case in which the notion of
realizability below is applied. The *local characteristic
factor* of $\mathcal F$ at a closed point $x$ is

$$
P_x(T):=\prod_{\alpha\in S_x}(1-\alpha T)=\det(1-TF_x\mid V_x),
$$

where $S_x$ is the spectrum of $F_x$ counted with multiplicity.
The sheaf $\mathcal F$ is *$\iota$-real* if
$\iota(P_x(T))\in\mathbf R[T]$ for every closed point $x\in|X_0|$;
equivalently, the multiset of complex Frobenius eigenvalues is stable
under complex conjugation at every closed point. The sheaf $\mathcal F$
is *$\iota$-realizable* if it is a direct summand (in the category
of Weil sheaves) of an $\iota$-real lisse Weil sheaf
(*Deligne, Weil II, (1.2.13)*).

Here $\det(1-TF_x\mid V_x)$ is the reverse characteristic polynomial
of [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial], in the polynomial ring
$\Qlb[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The multiset $S_x$ consists of the
roots of $\chi_{F_x}$ [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial], each repeated
its algebraic root multiplicity [def-weil-root-multiplicity].
The notation $\iota(P_x)$ means applying $\iota$ to every coefficient;
its membership in $\mathbf R[T]$ means that every resulting complex
coefficient has imaginary part zero. Complex conjugation sends $a+bi$
to $a-bi$ for $a,b\in\mathbf R$. Lisse refers to the underlying
common-stage object being lisse of finite rank as in
[def-real-common-stage-lisse], on $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
Explicitly, direct summand means that there are a constructible Weil
sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $X_0$ and morphisms of Weil sheaves
$i:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ and $r:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ with
$r\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal F}$, where $\mathcal G$ is
lisse and $\iota$-real. No Frobenius-stable integral lattice is required.

The stalk Frobenius modules of the $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ are
computed at a finite coefficient stage, and $P_x$ does not depend on the
choices made. By the colimit description of morphisms of
$D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the Weil
isomorphism of $\mathcal F$, its inverse and the two equations saying
that they are mutually inverse are represented over one finite
extension $E\in\mathcal E_\ell$; hence $\mathcal F$ is isomorphic, as a
Weil sheaf, to the image $(E,(\mathcal F_E,\theta_E))$ of an $E$-Weil
sheaf as in part 4 of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. For a closed point
$x$, a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$ and the associated
geometric point $\bar x$, take $V_x=\Qlb\otimes_E\mathcal
H^0(\mathcal F_E)_{\bar x}$ and $F_x=\Qlb\otimes_EF_x^{E}$, where
$F_x^{E}$ is the local geometric Frobenius of
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Two finite presentations of
$\mathcal F$ and two embeddings give operators that are conjugate by a
$\Qlb$-linear isomorphism [lem-wf-adic-local-frobenius-model-conjugacy];
conjugate endomorphisms have the same reverse characteristic polynomial,
so $P_x$, and hence $\iota$-reality, is independent of these choices.

lean.note: Section 1(B): the recorded AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsRealizable accepts the older WeilSheaf over PadicAlgCl, not the recorded sfCommonStageWeilSheaf of def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex. It therefore does not supply the local characteristic factors needed by d-real-cohom on that heart. This module defines the determinant on the recorded finite-stage local Frobenius stalk, descends it by its unique all-presentation characterization, and states the reality and lisse-retract realizability predicates for the actual common-stage Weil heart. No sheaf, stalk operator or local polynomial is chosen from a mere unstructured existence assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q70-4df0bd58b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, the report, all 8 stmt_deps, blueprint master/main-20261015/main-20261017 and Deligne Weil II (1.2.12)-(1.2.14) (PDF pp.19-23). The statement keeps every blueprint clause and adds correct clarifications: the Weil-equivariant retract r∘i=id, lisse in the sense of def-real-common-stage-lisse with no Weil-stable lattice (this matches Deligne 1.2.14 for Weil sheaves), and coefficientwise ι. Removing the base proof is right. Its step 1 cited a 'complex_descent' clause that lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior does not contain (C4), and a definition carries no proof. One fault, repaired (C4 / claim inside a definition, stages/1-dag §2). The delivery also dropped the only link to lem-wf-adic-local-frobenius-model-conjugacy, which was created for this item: its blueprint.from is 'independence of the finite coefficient presentation and residue embedding'. After the delivery nothing cites that node. The item is about a Q̄_ℓ common-stage sheaf, and def-weil-punctual-weights takes F_y from def-weil-local-frobenius-trace, which works only at a finite stage E. Its only independence citation covers a change of embedding at fixed E, so P_x had no well-definedness theorem. Repair, in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-purity-real-sheaves/def-wf-iota-real.json: one statement paragraph. First, it presents F at a finite E through the colimit Hom of def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients and part 4 of def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex. Second, it sets V_x=Q̄_ℓ⊗H^0(F_E)_x̄ with the scalar-extended F_x^E. Third, it takes independence of presentation and embedding from lem-wf-adic-local-frobenius-model-conjugacy (its hypotheses are met: separated X₀, j=0, no heart condition), and conjugate operators have the same det(1−TF). Three stmt_deps are added. I checked there is no cycle and all other fields are unchanged. Edge cases checked: V=0, eigenvalues {i}, {i,−i}, a Jordan block, the zero sheaf, empty X₀. The 'equivalently' clause is elementary because the eigenvalues α are nonzero. There are no new nodes and no tool_uses.
